home.title: {siteName} — A sensory trail for blind and visually impaired people, Sacred Valley of the Incas
home.description: An educational and sensory trail being developed for blind and visually impaired people, with their families, friends and companions, in the Sacred Valley of the Incas, Cusco, Peru.
home.heroAlt: Poster of the project. A person in a poncho and Andean hat walks with a white cane along a stone path with a rope handrail, between Inca stone walls and an arch, with Andean terraces and snow-capped mountains behind. Stone signs along the path carry Braille dots. The poster reads: THE INCA BRAILLE TRAIL — GUIDING FOOTSTEPS THROUGH HISTORY. A stone sign reads: INCA TRAIL & Braille.
home.tagline: An educational and sensory trail for blind and visually impaired people, in the Sacred Valley of the Incas, Cusco, Peru.

boxes.title: What Is the Inca Braille Trail?

content.lead: A Journey Through Nature, Education and the Senses

content: Located in the beautiful Sacred Valley of the Incas, Cusco, Peru, the Inca Braille Trail is an educational and sensory experience being developed specifically for blind and visually impaired people, together with their families, friends and companions.
Our vision is to create a welcoming place where visitors can enjoy nature, learn, explore and share meaningful experiences, free of charge through the support of sponsors and donations.

The trail is designed to stimulate the senses through touch, smell, sound and taste. Visitors will discover the textures of plants, the fragrances of herbs and flowers, the sounds of nature and the many wonderful experiences the natural world has to offer.

boxes.title: The Cycle of Life – Learning from Pachamama
content: At the heart of our philosophy is respect for Pachamama, Mother Earth, and the understanding that all living things are connected.
Through our educational journey, The Cycle of Life, visitors will discover how the needs of plants closely reflect our own.
A tiny seed needs nourishment, water, warmth and care to grow, just as we need nutritious food, clean water, sunlight and a healthy environment to thrive.
Plants draw nutrients from healthy soil and energy from sunlight, while we depend on the food they produce for our own energy, growth and wellbeing.

content.lead: Healthy soil nurtures healthy plants. Healthy plants nourish healthy people.

content: Animals also play an essential role in this cycle. From honeybees pollinating flowers to birds spreading seeds, and farm animals providing natural manure that enriches the soil, every creature contributes to the balance of nature.
These nutrients return to the earth, helping new plants grow and completing the beautiful cycle that connects plants, animals and people.

Along the journey, visitors will explore traditional Andean and ancient Inca agricultural practices alongside modern sustainable farming. We emphasize the importance of preserving native seeds, composting, protecting biodiversity and growing nutritious food without relying on harmful agricultural chemicals.
Our goal is to demonstrate that caring for the earth and producing healthy food can be simple, sustainable and accessible to everyone.

boxes.title: A Place for Everyone to Connect – The Spirit of Ayni
content: At the heart of the Inca Braille Trail is the ancient Andean principle of Ayni, meaning reciprocity — the belief that through giving, receiving and supporting one another, we create stronger, more compassionate communities.

Our trail is more than an educational experience. It is a place where blind and visually impaired people, their families, friends and companions can come together, share experiences, build friendships and celebrate life.
We also hope to encourage sighted visitors to better understand the everyday challenges faced by people with visual impairments, developing greater awareness, empathy and respect.
Through shared experiences, we want people to recognize that everyone has something valuable to offer and that we all have something to learn from one another.
Just as we nurture the earth and the earth nurtures us, through kindness, compassion and reciprocity, we nurture one another.

content.lead: This is the spirit of Ayni, and the heart of the Inca Braille Trail.

volunteer.title: Volunteer — {siteName}
volunteer.description: Volunteers urgently needed: clearing and shaping trails, moving stones, gardening and grounds maintenance. Meals provided; accommodation for full-day volunteers.
volunteer.lead: Volunteers urgently needed to open the trail to blind and visually impaired visitors.

boxes.title: Help build the trail
content: Volunteers urgently needed! Help bring the Inca Braille Trail to life by creating welcoming paths and caring for our beautiful grounds.

Tasks include clearing and shaping trails, moving stones, gardening and general grounds maintenance. Your contribution will help open this sensory experience to blind and visually impaired visitors and their companions.

list: Volunteers staying with us and working full days: Accommodation, breakfast, lunch and dinner provided.
Transport: Available from an agreed collection point.

content: Contact us to arrange dates and find tasks suited to your abilities.
